content: 1. The National Federation's website, hosted by OMICS International in Hyderabad in 2021, provides information on various associations, including the Thalassaemia International Federation. This resource was accessed on February 1, 2022. 2. Eleftheriou A. authored a comprehensive guide titled About Thalassaemia, published by the Thalassaemia International Federation in Nicosia in 2007. This document, available online, was accessed on February 1, 2022. 3. A website dedicated to specialized nutritious foods offers detailed information on their development and use. This resource was accessed on February 1, 2022. 4. The Corn Soy Blend/Plus Commodity Fact Sheet, available on a government website, provides insights into the nutritional benefits and applications of this fortified food product. This document was accessed on February 1, 2022. 5. Seal A. and colleagues conducted a study demonstrating that fortification of maize meal is associated with improved vitamin A and iron status in adolescents and a reduction in childhood anemia within food aid-dependent refugee populations. The findings were published in the journal Public Health Nutrition in 2008 (Volume 11, Pages 720–728). 6. The World Health Organization's ExpandNet initiative outlines nine steps for developing a scaling-up strategy for health interventions. This document was accessed on February 1, 2022. 7. The WHO Handbook on Health Inequality Monitoring, with a focus on lowand middle-income countries, provides a framework for assessing and addressing health disparities. This resource was accessed on February 1, 2022. 8. Garcia-Casal MN and colleagues reviewed the fortification of maize flour with iron as a strategy to control anemia and iron deficiency in populations. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2018 (Issue 12, Article CD010187). 9. The eCatalogue of Indicators for Micronutrient Programmes is an online database that provides standardized metrics for evaluating micronutrient interventions. This resource was accessed on February 1, 2022. 10. The Micronutrients Database, part of the Vitamin and Mineral Nutrition Information System (VMNIS), offers comprehensive data on global micronutrient deficiencies and interventions. This database was accessed on February 1, 2022. 11. The Global Targets Tracking Tool, developed by the World Health Organization in 2021, enables monitoring of progress toward global nutrition targets. This tool was accessed on February 1, 2022. 12. The WHO Global Nutrition Targets 2025: Anemia Policy Brief outlines strategies to reduce anemia prevalence worldwide. This document was accessed on February 1, 2022. 13. The Global Database on the Implementation of Nutrition Action (GINA) is an online platform that tracks the implementation of nutrition policies and programs globally. This database was accessed on February 1, 2022. 14. The WHO Expert Advisory Panels and Committees website provides information on the organization's collaborative efforts with global experts. This resource was accessed on February 1, 2022. 15. A supplement issue of the Food and Nutrition Bulletin focuses on evidence-based approaches to flour fortification and strategies for advancing this public health intervention. This publication was accessed on February 1, 2022. 16. Higgins J. and Green S., editors of the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, provide guidelines for conducting high-quality systematic reviews. The handbook was updated in March 2011 and accessed on February 1, 2022. 17. The International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) is an online database that consolidates information on clinical trials conducted worldwide. This platform was accessed on February 1, 2022. 18. The WHO Guidelines for Declaration of Interests for Experts outline ethical standards for transparency and conflict of interest management. This document was accessed on February 1, 2022. 19. The GRADE Working Group provides a framework for assessing the quality of evidence in systematic reviews and guidelines. Evidence is categorized into high, moderate, low, or very low certainty based on factors such as study design, risk of bias, and consistency of results. 20. Studies included in meta-analyses are evaluated for limitations in study design, indirectness of evidence, inconsistency of results, and imprecision of estimates. These factors influence the confidence in the estimated effects of interventions. 21. Fortification of wheat flour with vitamins and minerals is recommended as a public health strategy to address micronutrient deficiencies. Evidence supporting this intervention is graded based on the GRADE framework, with considerations for study quality and relevance to target populations. 22. Specific studies, such as those by Amalrajan (2012) and Muthayya (2012), contribute to the evidence base for wheat flour fortification. However, limitations in study design and execution, as well as variability in baseline anemia prevalence, affect the overall confidence in the findings. 23. The effectiveness of fortified foods, such as chapatis made with fortified wheat flour, has been evaluated in specific populations, including children aged 6 to 15 years. Supervised food intake ensures adherence to the intervention. 24. Studies on zinc deficiency and its correction through fortified foods highlight the importance of addressing micronutrient deficiencies in vulnerable populations, such as children and women of reproductive age. 25. The interpretation of findings from studies with high risk of bias or limited generalizability requires caution. For example, studies with high attrition rates or lack of randomization may not provide reliable evidence. 26. The direction and magnitude of effects observed in studies on fortified foods vary, underscoring the need for high-quality research to inform public health strategies. 27. The WHO guidelines emphasize the importance of fortifying staple foods, such as wheat flour, with essential vitamins and minerals to improve population health outcomes. These guidelines are based on systematic reviews and expert consensus.
